stories.title: Iran launches strikes on Jordan after US attacks an island in Hormuz
stories.summary: The US attacks on Iran are the first in around a month as the Trump administration had shifted its war objective to inflict maximum economic pain on Tehran. Washington says the strikes were aimed at preventing Iranian forces from disrupting global shipping through the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: Mauled Australian swimmer recalls punching shark at Sydney beach
stories.summary: An Australian school teacher mauled by a large shark at a Sydney beach says she fired a “left hook” at the predator before it dragged her underwater. Leah Stewart, a primary school teacher, was placed in an induced coma and had part of her left arm amputated after the June 13 attack at Sydney’s Coogee Beach. Stewart decided to go for a late morning swim in the “crystal clear” sea, unknowingly sharing the water with a shark described by witnesses as a great white measuring up to 4m long. The teacher said she was finishing her swim and approaching the sand when she heard a girl scream. “I turned, and there was a huge, huge fin behind her. It was massive, and at first I thought, ‘Oh, it’s a dolphin’,” she told. Nine Network television’s 60 Minutes in a program aired on Aug 30. “I looked at the size of it and I realised, that’s not a dolphin. And so we just start screaming at the top of our lungs, just like ‘shark, shark, shark’.” She swam a few more strokes, then felt something in the water, and turned around to see it slowly approaching. “Its face was horrific. I’ll never forget its face, it was huge.

stories.title: Prosecutors seek 10-yr sentence for Pakistani man in child rape case
stories.summary: Prosecutors have sought a heavy sentence for a Pakistani national indicted for sexually assaulting foreign children nearly two decades earlier at an Islamic mosque in Incheon, west of Seoul, judicial officials said Monday. Prosecutors asked the Bucheon branch of the Incheon District Court to sentence the unidentified Pakistani man to 10 years in prison on charges including rape of minors under the age of 13, during a hearing in mid-July, the officials said. The man is accused of threatening and sexually assaulting two foreign children, then aged seven and nine, at a mosque in Incheon's Seohae district in September 2008. He was teaching the Quran at the mosque at the time. Prosecutors said a complaint was filed belatedly because the victims were too young at the time of the incident.
